text:
maya: FYI we just got an escalation from AcmeCorp — their p99 latency for /v1/generate jumped ~3x starting ~02:15 UTC. p95 looks fine in the dashboard but p99 is spiking to ~1.8s intermittently. Customer provided a trace and a screenshot: https://redwood.internal/attachments/ACME/trace-002.png :grimacing:
ellie (oncall): thanks, pinging eng-sre and obs. can you paste the query you used to get the p99 from their dashboard?

maya (support): dashboard panel (Grafana) uses the pre-aggregated metric `service.request_duration_seconds_rollup` with quantile=0.99 and window=5m. I also ran a raw histogram query from metrics-service and saw slightly different numbers: `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))` — that returned ~900ms at the same time series window.

samir (sre): interesting. so dashboard rollup shows 1.8s, raw histogram shows 0.9s. that smells like aggregation/rollup bucket aliasing or different bucketing. can you dump the bucket boundaries?

kai (observability): I pulled the two series. rollup metric is produced by metrics-aggregator which resamples to 20 buckets (log-scale) every 30s. raw histogram has 120 buckets (fine-grained). if you use coarse buckets and then compute quantiles from those, you can get a heavier tail — especially when requests have a bimodal distribution.

ellie (oncall): quick check: is the dashboard using `quantile_over_time` or relying on the rollup's precomputed quantile?

maya (support): dashboard panel uses the precomputed field `p99` emitted by metrics-aggregator. i can switch panel to run live `histogram_quantile` against raw buckets but that's heavier. customer is unhappy now though.

samir (sre): can we reproduce locally? steps: 1) run `tools/loadgen` with a bimodal mix (90% short 80ms, 10% tail 1.5s) for 10k requests; 2) scrape raw histogram; 3) run rollup transform that compresses into 20 log buckets; 4) compute quantiles both ways. i suspect the rollup overstates p99 because the low-res buckets group the tail with higher le boundaries.

kai (observability): confirmed on my local sim. pasted results:
```
# local sim (10k requests, 90% 80ms, 10% 1.5s)
raw histogram p99 -> 0.92s
rollup-derived p99 -> 1.78s
```

monitoring-bot: alert: ACME /v1/generate p99 > 1.5s (fired) 02:21 UTC — routed to eng-oncall

ellie (oncall): ok, two-pronged short-term mitigation: (A) switch Grafana panel to use `histogram_quantile` on raw buckets (less biased), (B) temporarily silence the noisy p99 alert for this customer scope and create a separate alert on tail rate (requests>1s count) so we don't miss true regressions.

maya (support): i switched the panel to raw histogram query and updated Acme. they now see ~0.95s p99. i also notified them about potential delta due to rollup compression. :thumbsup:
samir (sre): longer-term we should: 1) update metrics-aggregator to preserve more bucket granularity for latency histograms (increase target buckets from 20 -> 80 for request latencies), 2) add a unit test in aggregator that compares rollup quantile vs histogram_quantile for synthetic workloads and flags >20% divergence, 3) add documentation on the dashboard about which panels use rollup vs raw. i'll open PRs.
kai (observability): opened tracking issue: https://redwood.internal/issues/OBS-4272 (notes + repro harness + perf cost estimate). also pushed a dashboard note that the rollup p99 is deprecated for SLA checks.
ellie (oncall): action items assigned:
- samir: PR to increase buckets + unit test (ETA EOD)
- kai: add dashboard note + link to issue (ETA today)
- maya: confirm with Acme that panel change resolves their concern and close escalation (ETA 1h)
- ellie: create temporary alert on tail-rate and silence rollup-p99 for the customer scope (done)

maya (support): Acme replied: "thanks, dashboard looks correct now and we've got reduced alerts. please keep us posted on permanent fix." closing loop. :relieved:
samir (sre): PR #842 merged to staging with bucket increase and test. rolling to prod tomorrow in a canary. i'll post more once rollout metrics look healthy.
kai (observability): note for followup — check billing impact of increasing rollup buckets (more data points). estimate +7% metric ingestion. file in finance review.
ellie (oncall): nice work team. summary for postmortem: apparent p99 regression was an observability artifact caused by coarse histogram rollup (20 buckets) + quantile calc on compressed buckets. mitigations: switched dashboard to raw histograms, increased rollup fidelity, added unit test, created tail-rate alert. leaving this thread open until prod canary completes. :white_check_mark:
